Remarks: 
1. Teaching and assessment for graduate students will proceed according to the suitability of each 
program. 
2. From Monday afternoon onward, all theoretical and practical classes are suspended. This period is 
reserved as an out-of-classroom learning day through extracurricular activities for undergraduate 
students. 
3. The teaching period is divided into two phases:  
o The ﬁrst phase (for Modules 1 and 2) includes 10 weeks of instruction, followed by an 
assessment period in Weeks 11-12. 
o Instruction then continues for another 5 weeks (Weeks 13-17), followed by an assessment 
period for Module 3 in Weeks 18-19. 
o General courses will align their teaching schedules with these periods to avoid overlapping 
with students' class times.

11 
 
4. Assessments for module courses:  
o Assessments for Modules 1 and 2 will follow the academic calendar schedule, with Module 1 
in Week 11 and Module 2 in Week 12. 
o Module 3 assessments will take place in Weeks 18-19. 
o For general courses, midterm assessments will occur in Weeks 11-12, and ﬁnal assessments in 
Weeks 18-19. 
5. Teaching and assessments during the Summer Semester will proceed as speciﬁed in this academic 
calendar. 
6. Course registration, late registration, adding, dropping, and withdrawing for both general and 
module courses must be completed within the periods speciﬁed in this academic calendar. 
7. Regulations for module courses are as follows:  
o a. The university allows students to take exams for module courses before deciding whether 
to withdraw. 
o b. Short-term modules will not announce assessment scores to students before the 
withdrawal deadline. 
8. For course withdrawals, the date the student submits a fully complete request is considered the 
conﬁrmed withdrawal date, even if the approval process in New ACIS is not yet complete. Once a 
withdrawal is approved, it cannot be canceled. If a student receives withdrawal approval before the 
exam date but still attends the exam (even if their name is on the exam list), the exam will be 
considered void, and the withdrawal cannot be reversed. 
9. Students on academic probation must obtain permission from their advisors before completing the 
ﬁnal step of registration. 
10. Students must clear any outstanding tuition fees from the previous semester before they can 
register for the next semester. 
11. If a student registers for courses but fails to pay tuition fees by the speciﬁed date in the calendar, 
the registered courses will be canceled. The student must then re-select courses during the 
registration period on the ﬁrst day of the semester. 
12. Students who register late or pay the status maintenance fee late will be subject to a ﬁne of 50 
THB per day (including holidays), counting from the ﬁrst day of the semester as speciﬁed in this 
academic calendar. 
13. Students with incomplete grades ("I") from the previous semester will not be permitted to register 
for the next semester. 
14. Students intending to take a leave of absence must complete the faculty approval process before 
the status maintenance registration deadline speciﬁed in this calendar. 
  
Announced on April 7, 2026 
 
(Associate Professor Dr. Suvit Saetia)  
President of the University 
 
Approved by the Academic Council on Tuesday, April 7, 2026

12 
 
Note: Recognizing the challenges arising from the university's diverse teaching and learning formats—including 
both general instruction and short-term modules that feature a single learning outcomes assessment at the 
end—this may cause concern among students, parents, and faculty regarding the potential results. Therefore, 
the university has comprehensively considered this matter and agreed that effective learning should be 
accompanied by fair opportunities for students to prove themselves. Consequently, the schedules for teaching, 
learning, and assessing learning outcomes have been adjusted. This adjustment emphasizes providing students 
with increased opportunities to fully explore their potential, alongside ﬂexibility and the full support of the 
university, to ensure that everyone can achieve their educational goals with the utmost conﬁdence.
